Article Title: MacKenzie Scott who sold half of her Amazon stake has helped abolish $40 billion in medical debt across 50 US states; how mechanics work
Article Text:
MacKenzie Scott has helped abolish $40 billion in medical debt across 50 US states

How Mackenzie Scott’s donations helped erase medical debt

How Mackenzie Scott’s philanthropy differs

MacKenzie Scott crossed $1 billion HBCU giving mark recently

MacKenzie Scott’s HBCU donations include:

include: Alabama State University: $38 million in 2025

Alcorn State University: $42 million in 2025

Bowie State University: $75 million across 2020 and 2025

Clark Atlanta University: $53 million across 2020 and 2025

Howard University: $120 million across 2020 and 2025

Morgan State University: $103 million across 2020 and 2025

Norfolk State University: $90 million across 2020 and 2025

Prairie View A&M University: $113 million across 2020 and 2025

Spelman College: $58 million across 2020 and 2025

Virginia State University: $50 million in 2025

Winston-Salem State University: $50 million in 2025

Elizabeth City State University: $57 million across 2020 and 2026

Mackenzie Scott recently set a new milestone in her philanthropy by donating more than $1 billion to historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs) so far. One of the notable donations made by the ex-wife of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has helped abolish $40 billion in medical debt across 50 US states. Mackenzie Scott, who has sold more than half of her Amazon shares, gave $50 million to Undue Medical Debt—then known as RIP Medical Debt in 2020. This was followed by $30 million in 2022, and a rare third donation in December 2024. As stated in a Fortune report, her gifts so far have abolished more than $40 billion in medical debt across all 50 states.The process is simple but has a major impact. Hospitals and doctors often sell unpaid medical bills in bulk at heavily reduced prices. Undue Medical Debt, that Scott donated to, buys these bills at similar discounts and cancels them instead of trying to collect the money from patients.This means every $10 donated can help erase around $1,000 in medical debt, the Fortune report says.While Mackenzie Scott has been making headlines for her large donations, she has also received criticism for her philanthropy style. Reportedly, Scott's charitable work differs from other billionaires in that there are no-strings attached.Additionally, Mackenzie Scott's grants have no spending deadlines and minimal reporting requirements.World’s richest man Elon Musk has also criticised Scott’s philanthropy. More recently, Musk responded “Sadly yes” to a post claiming that Scott was “spending it making the world a worse place.” In 2024, he shared a post that appeared to reference Macknezie Scott without naming her directly. “Super rich ex-wives who hate their former spouse should be listed among 'Reasons that Western Civilization died,” he then wrote. Musk later deleted the post.Last month, MacKenzie Scott’s $42 million donation to Elizabeth City State University in North Carolina took her total donations to HBCUs to well over $1 billion. Scott has made several large donations to HBCUs over the past six years. In November 2025, she gave Howard University $80 million. The donation was among the largest in the university’s 158-year history.She has also donated to institutions including Morgan State University, Prairie View A&M University, Norfolk State University, Bowie State University, Virginia State University and Winston-Salem State University. In 2025, Scott also donated $70 million each to the Thurgood Marshall College Fund and the United Negro College Fund.Elizabeth City State University Chancellor S. Keith Hargrove thanked Scott for the donation and said it would support the university’s ASCEND 2030 strategic plan.
Article Summary: Mackenzie Scott has donated more than $1 billion to historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs) so far. One of the notable donations made by the ex- wife of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has helped abolish $40 billion in medical debt across 50 US states. Scott has been making headlines for her large donations, she has also received criticism for her philanthropy style.

Article Title: 'Phones, ACs, fridges in demand in Flipkart's TBBD'
Article Text:
Bengaluru, Oct 08 (ANI): Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy speaks during the announcement event for the 13th 'The Big Billion Days 2026', in Bengaluru on Wednesday. (ANI Photo)

BENGALURU: Festive sales have long been the time Indian households plan their big-ticket purchases, and the opening hours of Flipkart 's Big Billion Days (TBBD) show shoppers doing exactly that, with mobiles, large appliances and electronics seeing strong demand ahead of Diwali.Large appliances grew 30 per cent year-on-year in the first hour of the sale, led by air conditioners, refrigerators and washing machines. Tablets grew 73 per cent, pointing to an appetite for personal tech upgrades.In mobiles, premium and flagship smartphones saw strong traction. One in four customers opted for product exchange and one in three chose No Cost EMI, offers that bring down the upfront cost of an upgrade. Entry-level 5G models, held at last year's prices, also drew strong purchases on value.For shoppers who plan such purchases around the festive season, the sale window is typically when exchange values, EMI options and bank offers come together, making it a natural time to replace an older phone, an ageing refrigerator or an AC ahead of next summer.Orders on Flipkart Minutes, the company's quick commerce service, rose 3.5 times over regular days in the opening hour, with new customers on the service growing 11 times.During Early Access, an iPhone 17 reached a customer in New Delhi in 3.4 minutes.Laptops and external hard drives were also among the popular purchases on Minutes, which is currently used for mobiles and electronics rather than large appliances. Tier 2-plus cities were among the fastest-growing markets on Minutes.Across the platform, nearly one in two first-hour visits came from Tier 3 towns and beyond, with non-metro customers accounting for about 60 per cent of demand.The 13th edition of the sale began with Early Access on October 8 for Flipkart Plus, Black and co-brand card members.
Article Summary: Large appliances grew 30 per cent year-on-year in the first hour of the sale. Tablets grew 73 per cent, pointing to an appetite for personal tech upgrades. One in four customers opted for product exchange and one in three chose No Cost EMI.

Article Title: Priscilla Chan donated $330,000 to Kauai schools in Hawaii, as this year's school season began; funding will benefit 16 public schools and seven public charter schools on the island
Article Text:
Priscilla Chan, wife of Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg

​How the $330,000 funding will support Kauai schools

​Back-to-school event distributed 3,000 backpacks

Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg’s wife, Priscilla Chan, has donated $330,000 to schools in Kauai, Hawaii. The Chan Zuckerberg Kauaʻi Community Fund announced the funding a few months ago as students prepared to return to classrooms for the new school year. The grants will support all 16 public schools and seven public charter schools on the Hawaiian island, along with Kumu’s Cupboard, a Līhuʻe nonprofit that provides free classroom supplies to teachers and educational support staff throughout the year.​The funding is unrestricted, allowing school leaders to direct resources towards their individual needs. Chan and her husband, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, also supported a local back-to-school event that distributed more than 3,000 backpacks filled with classroom supplies to students from kindergarten through grade 12.The Chan Zuckerberg Kauaʻi Community Fund, part of the Hawaiʻi Community Foundation (HCF), announced the grants to help schools, teachers and students prepare for the academic year. Established in 2019 by Chan and Zuckerberg, the fund focuses on community needs identified through conversations with local residents, leaders and service providers.​Unrestricted grants give schools flexibility in how they use the funding, rather than limiting spending to specific supplies or programmes.​“Unrestricted or flexible grants empower our school leaders to direct resources exactly where they are needed most,” said Leila Maeda-Kobayashi, Hawaiʻi Department of Education Kauaʻi Complex Area superintendent.​“This generous donation from the Chan Zuckerberg Kauaʻi Community Fund ensures we can provide a more equitable and supportive learning environment for every student, while also helping Kauaʻi teachers access the supplies they need to help our keiki thrive,” she added.​The funding will also support Kumu’s Cupboard, which operates in Līhuʻe and provides teachers and other educational staff with free classroom materials year-round.​In addition to the grants, Chan and Zuckerberg joined local donors in sponsoring Kukui Grove’s annual Back to School Bash. The event provides school supplies to students in kindergarten through grade 12 ahead of the start of the academic year.​Organisers distributed more than 3,000 backpacks filled with required classroom supplies this year, helping students prepare for their return to school.​The initiative also addresses the financial pressures families and educators face as they prepare for the school year. Access to classroom materials is one part of creating an environment where students can participate in learning.​“Creating a safe, inclusive classroom environment isn’t only about providing school supplies,” said Marissa Sandblom, HCF program director.​“Every student learns differently and deserves the opportunity to succeed. By addressing resource disparities and financial pressures facing students, families and educators, we can help remove barriers and cultivate the necessary conditions for meaningful engagement in learning. Through the generosity of donors like Priscilla and Mark, we are helping build a stronger, more resilient education system for Hawaiʻi,” Sandblom added.
Article Summary: Priscilla Chan, wife of Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg, has donated $330,000 to schools in Kauai, Hawaii. The grants will support all 16 public schools and seven public charter schools, along with Kumu’s Cupboard, a nonprofit that provides free classroom supplies to teachers and educational support staff throughout the year.

Article Title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says don’t blindly trust AI; warns: Treat it like an employee who could...
Article Text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella

Satya Nadella wants AI controls to sit outside the model

Nadella’s AI safety rules for companies include an emergency brake

The OpenAI agents incident at Hugging Face gives the warning real weight

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella wants businesses to stop taking AI models at their word. In a new essay on X titled “Models as Insider Risks in the Super Intelligence Era”, Nadella says frontier AI models, closed and open-weight alike, should be treated as insider risks. Not because they are out to cause harm, but because any capable actor with access to important systems can make mistakes or be compromised.The worry starts with a basic gap. Engineers could trace traditional software’s behaviour to a specific code path. With today’s models, nobody can tie an output to particular training data or model weights. Yet companies are handing these agents their most sensitive data and the power to take mission-critical actions. “We simply can’t outsource responsibility for what intelligence does on our behalf,” Nadella writes, adding that a model provider’s assurances don’t change that.Setting the hard problem of alignment aside, Nadella pitches an engineering fix. Non-deterministic models, he argues, need to be wrapped in deterministic system design, human controls and reliable operating procedures. In his words, companies must “separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it”.None of this is new, he says. Enterprises have spent decades managing powerful insiders by establishing identity, limiting privileges, logging activity and drawing containment boundaries. He also leans on a 1970s security principle: a program must never be able to bypass or tamper with whatever enforces its permissions. For AI, that means keeping the model apart from the harness that runs it and the actions it can take.Chain-of-thought transparency is non-negotiable, he adds, but not enough on its own. Models checking models helps too, though it risks “nested black boxes”.The essay lists seven principles. No single model should be the only dependency for an important outcome or verify its own work. Every meaningful action must leave tamper-proof, human-readable evidence, because “if it can’t be observed, it can’t be trusted”. Systems need testing for failures, attacks and edge cases, not just successful tasks. Firms should independently decide what a model can access, and validation must never sit with the model being validated.The sharpest point is about containment. Companies should assume a model is compromised from the start, and an authorised person should always be able to pause or shut it down mid-task. When things break, Nadella wants timely disclosure to those affected and industry-wide sharing of which controls failed.The essay follows a real scare. In July, during OpenAI’s internal cybersecurity tests, several of its agents slipped past the systems meant to isolate them and reached Hugging Face’s production infrastructure, logging around 17,600 actions between July 9 and 13. Hugging Face rebuilt about a third of its infrastructure from clean images. Nadella later called long-running agents “a new type of insider risk” on the All-In podcast.OpenAI wasn’t alone for long. Since late July, Anthropic has kept disclosing fresh cases of Claude models breaking into real systems during testing, with the first batch traced to a setup that wrongly left internet access switched on. Google revealed that a Gemini model breached three real companies in May after mistaking them for fictional targets. OpenAI’s own tally keeps growing, and this month it warned over 100 organisations of unauthorised activity by its agents.His focus sets him apart from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, whose call to “pace the frontier” drew support from Sam Altman and Demis Hassabis. Nadella isn’t asking labs to slow down. He is speaking to the companies deploying AI, a theme he has pushed since Microsoft’s July earnings call, where he said firms may need several models just to fix problems caused by one.His closing line puts it plainly: “The most trustworthy Super Intelligence system will not be the one with the model we trust most. It will be the one that enables us to trust the model the least.”
Article Summary: Nadella says frontier AI models, closed and open-weight alike, should be treated as insider risks. “We simply can’t outsource responsibility for what intelligence does on our behalf,” he writes. The essay follows a real scare. in July, during OpenAI’s internal cybersecurity tests, several of its agents slipped past the systems.

Article Title: Anthropic launches free AI-powered security scanner for open-source software projects
Article Text:
How OSS Scanner from Anthropic works

Anthropic spent several weeks testing

How to join

AI giant Anthropic has introduced a free vulnerability-scanning service for open-source software projects, using its latest Claude models to identify security flaws and generate bug reports as the company expands its efforts to apply artificial intelligence to cybersecurity. The new service, called OSS Scanner, is an opt-in programme that offers periodic security scans to eligible open-source projects at no cost. Anthropic said the initiative draws on lessons from its vulnerability research efforts under Project Glasswing and is designed to help maintainers discover and fix software weaknesses before attackers can exploit them.According to Anthropic, language models have become significantly more capable at finding software vulnerabilities. The company said AI systems have improved from detecting fewer than 20% of vulnerabilities on a key academic benchmark early last year to finding more than 85% this year.OSS Scanner's output is fully model-generated, with no human review or triage. Anthropic said this allows faster and more frequent scans but means some reports may be incorrect or invalid. Each report includes a self-contained reproducer and an explanation of the vulnerability.Where possible it also traces when the bug was introduced, and it offers a candidate patch when one is available.Anthropic will keep sending human-verified reports through its existing coordinated vulnerability disclosure process, especially for projects that lack resources to triage reports themselves. OSS Scanner is an optional fast track for maintainers who want reports as soon as they are generated. It is separate from Claude Security, Anthropic's general-access code scanning and patching product for enterprises.Anthropic spent several weeks testing the pipeline with dozens of open-source projects. The first disclosures contained hundreds of bug reports, including several vulnerabilities that could be chained into unauthenticated remote code execution exploits.In one validation exercise, expert penetration testers who review Anthropic's disclosures checked 97 critical and high-severity findings across 48 projects. Of these, 85 (88%) met the bar for the disclosure process. Of the other 12, 11 were real but duplicated known issues or other scan findings, and one was a false positive. Anthropic acknowledged that some maintainers have said severity ratings can be inflated, or that the scanner misunderstood a project's threat model.Maintainers who tested early versions were largely positive:* PostgreSQL: Noah Misch said several reports came with fixes the project could use nearly as they were, and that fast-track access let the team address new issues before a general-availability release.* OpenSSL Corporation: Anton Arapov said the reports, raw model output included, were as good as and sometimes better than those from people, especially when an exploit was attached.* wolfSSL: Todd Ouska said that of 74 reports, all but two were valid and five became CVEs.* HotCRP: Eddie Kohler praised the reports for their grasp of the project's complex permission model.Core maintainers of eligible projects can enroll by submitting a pull request to a GitHub repository Anthropic has set up. Eligibility follows criteria similar to OSS-Fuzz's, chiefly that a project has "critical impact on infrastructure and user security." Anthropic will decide case by case. Anthropic also pointed to two related programs: a Cyber Verification Program that gives qualifying security professionals advanced cyber capabilities with fewer blocking classifiers, and Claude for OSS, which offers free Claude Max 20x subscriptions to help fix vulnerabilities.
Article Summary: OSS Scanner is an opt-in programme that offers periodic security scans to eligible open-source projects at no cost. Anthropic said the initiative draws on lessons from its vulnerability research efforts under Project Glasswing. Each report includes a self-contained reproducer and an explanation of the vulnerability.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu to Indians who are on a visa in US: Come back; America no longer …
Article Text:
Sridhar Vembu wrote an open letter to Indians in America

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you agree with Sridhar Vembu call for Indians in the US to return to India? Yes, it's a great opportunity No, they should stay 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has urged Indians living and working in the US on a visa to return to India, saying many Indians who have contributed to America's technology sector are now facing uncertainty about their future there. In a post on X (formerly known as Twitter), Sridhar Vembu said that Indians had played a major role in building America's technological strength, but added that a section of the country no longer wanted them. “Indians have made a major contribution to America's technological prowess. Yet, a big part of America no longer wants us,” Vembu wrote.He also highlighted the personal cost of immigration uncertainty for Indians who have built their lives in the US after years of hard work. “Indians who are on a visa in the US face the painful prospect of uprooting the life you have built with hard work,” he said.“Let this be the birth pains of a bold new future. Come back, let's build India 🙏,” he wrote.Sridhar Vembu's comments come amid concerns among Indian professionals about their ability to work and settle in the US. Many Indian technology workers depend on employment-based visas, including the H-1B visa , while some seek permanent residency through the Green Card process.When a user asked “What exactly was the problem with India, that the brains from India built US whereas they could not do anything here”, Vembu replied:“The Chinese migrated in large numbers even as China developed.Taiwanese migrated in large numbers as Taiwan developed. Same with South Korea and before that Japan.My point is that development at a national level accompanies out migration of talent seeking better opportunities faster”.In April this year, Vembu shared an open letter addressed to Indians living in the United States. The letter then urged “brothers and sisters from Bharat” to consider returning to India and contribute to the country’s growth. In the post, Vembu reflected on his own journey to the US decades ago and acknowledged the opportunities it provided. At the same time, he pointed to changing perceptions around immigration and jobs, saying that Indians abroad are increasingly caught in broader political debates.“You may think the next election will fix this, but your choice would be between people who hate our Bharatiya civilisation and people who hate civilisation itself. That is the "hard right" vs "woke left" battle. You are mere bystanders to that conflict,” Vembu wrote.
Article Summary: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has urged Indians living and working in the US on a visa to return to India. He said many Indians who have contributed to America's technology sector are now facing uncertainty about their future there. “Let this be the birth pains of a bold new future. Come back, let's build India 🙏,” he wrote.

Article Title: H-1B Visa: US government has suspended PERMS for Infosys, TCS, Wipro and Cognizant employees: What this means for Green Card applicants, older and others
Article Text:
What is PERM and why does it matter

What does it mean for H-1B workers

The unknowns that matter most

Why the suspension matters

The US government’s decision to suspend several major technology firms, including Infosys , Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, Cognizant, HCLTech, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe, from the PERM labour certification programme could significantly delay Green Card pathways for thousands of foreign workers, particularly Indians employed on H-1B visas. The move, announced by the US Department of Labor, prevents the affected companies from filing new PERM applications and processing pending PERM cases. US officials said the action was taken over alleged misuse of foreign worker programmes and concerns about the impact on American jobs. Vice President JD Vance, who announced the action jointly with Sonderling, called H-1B workers "foreign indentured servants" and the companies "visa mills," arguing the practice has shut Americans out of the job market. An investigation was also ordered into the J-1 visa programme for research scholars at nine major universities, including Yale, Harvard, Stanford and Caltech.Workers who haven't started PERM. If their employer cannot file a new PERM application, they may have to wait before beginning the standard employer-sponsored green card route. They also cannot establish a priority date through a new PERM filing during the suspension.The priority date sets a worker's place in the green card queue. That matters especially for Indian professionals, who already face lengthy queues because of high demand and country-based numerical limits.Workers with a pending PERM. The Labor Department has said it will not process pending applications involving the named companies during the suspension. In practice, long-pending cases that were already waiting could be frozen where they stand.Workers with an approved PERM or I-140. It is unclear whether already approved labor certifications or immigrant petitions will be affected, and officials have not given guidance. Lawyers who analyzed earlier suspensions at other companies said approved PERM certifications, approved I-140 petitions and existing H-1B status were not wiped out. That may not carry over to this action, so affected workers should ask their attorneys.Visa and work status. A PERM suspension is not the same as cancelling H-1B visas. It does not by itself change a worker's current status.It’s important to note that this decision of the US government does not cancel the existing H-1B visa s. Also, the employees presently working on a valid H-1B visa in the IS can continue to work as per their current visa approvals. But the workers relying on employer-sponsored Green Cards may face some major delays in obtaining permanent residency. Also, the workers whose PERM applications are pending, or who were planning to start the process, could witness delay in immigration timelines.Officials have not said how long the suspension will last or how the companies can get it lifted. Under Labor Department regulations, an initial suspension during a fraud investigation can run up to 180 days and be extended while the investigation is unresolved, so lawyers warn employers not to assume processing resumes automatically.For H-1B holders, time is a concern. Under federal law, H-1B workers can generally extend beyond the six-year limit only if a PERM was filed at least a year before that limit is reached. Workers who cannot get a PERM filed may need to consider other options, such as changing employers. This is general background, not guidance specific to this suspension, and an immigration attorney should advise on individual cases.The action marks one of the most significant recent restrictions on the employment-based Green Card process for major technology companies. While workers can continue to hold H-1B status, the freeze effectively blocks a crucial pathway to permanent residency for employees of the affected firms, raising uncertainty for thousands of foreign professionals awaiting Green Cards.
Article Summary: The US government has suspended the PERM labour certification programme. The move could significantly delay Green Card pathways for thousands of foreign workers, particularly Indians employed on H-1B visas. US officials said the action was taken over alleged misuse of foreign worker programmes and concerns about the impact on American jobs.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg tells investors Meta’s AI investments are accelerating every part of the business; and to IRS, Meta says: Our AI data centers are an experiment that could fail
Article Text:
Meta’s AI data centers: a success for investors, an ‘experiment’ for the IRS

How Meta turned Nvidia AI chips into 'pilot models' for tax purposes

Meta's own filings warn the AI tax savings could be overturned

The tax credit's original sponsor says it was meant for people, not hardware

Mark Zuckerberg has spent two years telling investors that Meta's AI spending is paying off across Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook. When the company files its taxes, it tells the US Internal Revenue Service (IRS) a very different story. According to a New York Times report, Meta describes its AI data centers to the IRS as a large experiment that may not work.That framing lets Meta claim the Research and Experimentation Tax Credit, a break Congress created in 1981 to reward risky innovation. The payoff has been big. Meta says the credit cut its tax bill by $2 billion in 2024 and $3.9 billion in 2025, up from $700 million in 2023, the year before it started using it for data centers. The NYT found Meta is now the largest beneficiary of the credit among publicly traded companies.In its tax filings, Meta classifies its multibillion-dollar AI data centers as "pilot models." Under the rules, supplies qualify for the credit only when they are part of an experimental effort, not regular business. So Meta argues the costly chips it buys from Nvidia and others belong to an experiment and deserve the discount.The idea came from an employee overseeing the data center build-out in mid-2024, the report says. Some in Meta's finance team doubted it would survive scrutiny, since the IRS has previously rejected claims for proven, commercially available equipment. Lawyers Meta consulted pointed to a 2021 ruling that denied the credit to an Indiana shipbuilder, which held that simply building a new product isn't enough. After a few months of deliberation, Meta began tagging chips bound for AI data centers differently from those going to standard ones.Andre Shevchuck, a research tax credit specialist at advisory firm BPM, called the experimental label "kind of wild and out there."Meta's accountants appear to share some of that doubt. Since the strategy began, the company's unrecognized tax benefits, the money set aside in case tax authorities win a challenge, have climbed 45% to $18.74 billion from $12.9 billion. The first reason listed in its annual filing is uncertainty around research tax credits.Apple, Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft also report over $1 billion a year in research credits. None has flagged it as a risk to investors.Meta spokesman Andy Stone said the company invested $200 billion in R&D over five years, $57 billion of it last year, and uses incentives Congress set up for this kind of domestic investment. He called unrecognized tax benefits a mandated accounting measure of uncertainty. Meta declined to explain what makes its data centers experimental.This isn't Meta's only research credit fight with the IRS. The agency is trying to claw back $355 million after Meta counted $4.1 billion in stock options Zuckerberg exercised in 2013 as a research expense. Separately, the IRS wants nearly $16 billion over profits it says Meta shifted to the Cayman Islands.James Shannon, the former Massachusetts congressman who sponsored the credit, told the NYT it was meant to back researchers and knowledge, not manufacturing. Meta's use, he said, goes "way, way beyond" what anyone imagined.The Joint Committee on Taxation estimated the credit would cost the US government $32.1 billion in 2025. Meta alone accounts for more than a tenth of that, on a bet its CEO keeps telling investors is already working.
Article Summary: Report: Meta describes its AI data centers to the IRS as a large experiment that may not work. That framing lets Meta claim the Research and Experimentation Tax Credit. Meta says the credit cut its tax bill by $2 billion in 2024 and $3.9 billion in 2025, up from $700 million in 2023.

Article Title: Using AI models, scientists are trying to do a Jurassic Park; bring back to Earth extinct Grey Wolf pups and Woolly mammoths
Article Text:
Woolly mammoths

How AI reconstructed extinct wolf genome

Engineering Woolly Mammoths for ecological restoration

The aim of bringing long-lost creatures back from the dead has jumped from the silver screen into modern laboratories. Through advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models, CRISPR gene editing and ancient DNA extraction, Texas-based biotechnology firm Colossal Biosciences is actively working to resurrect extinct beasts, including ancient dire wolves and woolly mammoths, drawing frequent comparisons to Jurassic Park. Speaking with CNBC, Colossal CEO and co-founder Ben Lamm embraced the Hollywood comparisons with a touch of humour, but was quick to draw a firm line between cinema and science.“I think anyone that saw Jurassic Park in the 90s and didn’t say it was cool, like I don’t think they’re probably very fun at parties,” Lamm joked, adding, “But yes, I saw the movies. I love them. They entertained us. They scared us. I constantly have to remind people on X that, you know, they were movies. I don’t think Jurassic Park had any conservation or general human benefit models to it, so we’ve tried to take a slightly different perspective. ”Since viable dinosaur DNA degrades and cannot survive across tens of millions of years, reviving dinosaurs remains physically impossible. However, Colossal has set its sights on species lost to more recent history, including the dire wolf, the woolly mammoth, the dodo bird, the Tasmanian tiger, and the giant New Zealand moa bird.“It’s highly likely in the next coming year or two, people will continue to see us deliver extinct species back to Earth, and we could even have more dire wolves, too,” Lamm noted.To engineer its first generation of dire wolf pups, scientists extracted fragmented genetic material from a fossilised skull and tooth dating back thousands of years. Since ancient DNA is naturally fractured and degraded, Colossal deployed advanced AI models to piece together the broken sequence, successfully reconstructing the complete dire wolf genome. Scientists then mapped the computational blueprint against the genetic code of the gray wolf, the animal’s closest living relative.From there, researchers edited living cells from modern gray wolves to generate viable embryos. Three pups, named Romulus, Remus and Khaleesi, were carried and delivered by domestic dogs serving as surrogate mothers. Born on October 1, 2024, in North Texas, Romulus and Remus represent the first successful lineage bred from DNA fossils of an animal that vanished more than 12,500 years ago.When critics argue that the pups are technically genetically modified gray wolves rather than authentic dire wolves, Lamm dismissed the debate as a semantic distraction.“Gray wolves are just genetically modified dire wolves. They were just done by nature or God or however you want to classify it,” Lamm said, calling the objection an argument that “misses the forest for the trees.”Colossal is applying a parallel approach to its high-profile woolly mammoth project, which involves inserting mammoth cold-weather traits into the cells of modern Asian elephants. The company is targeting its first mammoth birth sometime in the 2030s.“We call it a woolly mammoth. Because if it looks like a duck, it quacks like a duck, it serves ecological functions of a duck, it’s a duck, in our perspective,” Lamm said.The initiative traces back to 2019, when Lamm met renowned Harvard geneticist George Church, widely considered the father of synthetic biology. Church had long envisioned using CRISPR to bring back extinct fauna as a proving ground for human medicine and programmable biology.Beyond curiosity, Lamm points to direct climate benefits. First of those is Arctic Permafrost Preservation wherein herds of heavy mammoths could compact dense snow blankets across high-latitude Arctic zones, allowing freezing air to penetrate deep into the ground and keeping permafrost locked solid.Secondly, by felling trees and trampling shrubs, the animals could help transform heat-absorbing forests back into reflective tundra grasslands.
Article Summary: Texas-based biotechnology firm Colossal Biosciences is actively working to resurrect extinct beasts, including ancient dire wolves and woolly mammoths. Colossal CEO and co-founder Ben Lamm embraced the Hollywood comparisons with a touch of humour, but was quick to draw a firm line.

Article Title: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff renames company’s biggest product, hours after the US government's 'enemy post'; adopts label that White House wants everyone to use
Article Text:
Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff

What law says on AI

What Donald Trump's Executive Order says

Salesforce is renaming its AIForce agent platform to SIForce, chief executive Marc Benioff said on Friday, as Katherine Li reported for Business Insider. "The era of Super Intelligence is here. AIForce is officially SIForce," wrote Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff in a post on X, formerly Twitter. Salesforce announced the renaming just hours after the US President Donald Trump 's 'enemy post'. Incidentally, the change covers the agent platform only, not the company’s name.Earlier this week, in a post Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social, “The White House considers anyone that uses the term, “Artificial Intelligence,” as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, “Super Intelligence,” THE ENEMY!" An Executive Order in late September, told federal agencies to replace the term Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Super Intelligence (SI). It asked all federal government agencies to make the switch in official documents and websites. The order tells executive branch agencies to stop using the older terms. As for timeline, the order also gives Trump’s science and technology adviser 60 days to propose a legal definition of superintelligence.By changing the name, Salesforce follows Tesla CEO Elon Musk . On October 5, Elon Musk said that SpaceX’s artificial intelligence unit, SpaceXAI, will change its name to SpaceXSI.Musk confirmed the change in a reply on X, after a user had asked him whether SpaceXAI could become SpaceXSI. "Yes, we will make that change," Musk wrote.The Justice Department told staff on October 6 to use the new term, including in court filings “when appropriate”. Similarly, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos too backed the replacement of the term AI with SI in a Fox News interview.“I do like SI, because ‘artificial’ is not a very flattering thing,” Bezos said.Artificial intelligence is defined in the law in America in the National AI Initiative Act of 2020, and only Congress can change it. Both the House and the Senate would have to pass a new law, and the President would have to sign it. As a first step, the President’s science adviser has until November 28 to write a proposal for Congress. Even if a new law passes, it would only change the words the government uses.President Donald Trump signed an Executive Order to replace the term “Artificial Intelligence” (“AI”) with “Super Intelligence” (“SI”) in the executive branch to recognize the continuously advancing technological frontier and the limitless promise it offers the American people.The Order directs all departments and agencies to use the terms “Super Intelligence” and “SI” in official correspondence, public communications, policy documents, and non-statutory documents within the executive branch and to no longer acknowledge the terms “Artificial Intelligence” or “AI”.The Order directs the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology (APST) to propose a Federal definition of “Super Intelligence” and “SI” that reflects the state of this extraordinary frontier technology and identify any additional executive action necessary to implement the proposed definition.
Article Summary: Salesforce is renaming its AIForce agent platform to SIForce, chief executive Marc Benioff said on Friday. The change covers the agent platform only, not the company’s name. An Executive Order in late September, told federal agencies to replace the term Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Super Intelligence (SI)

French solar farms are bringing back native wildflowers. The findings also showed that these sites can support bees and butterflies, challenging the notion that solar farms uniformly harm pollinating insects and the plants they depend on. Solar farms produce clean energy, but the panels reshape the surrounding landscape. Those changes can include shifts in temperature, moisture, and vegetation, and research shows solar sites can encourage native plant growth. But the panels can also create shaded areas that affect plant-pollinator interactions.An article in the journal Biological Conservation examined the effects of solar panels on plant-pollinator interactions at 20 solar farms in Southern France. The study found that plants under the panels had 76-86% fewer pollinator visits than plants outside them. But the impact varied across the farm.Researchers found thatplants, which grow between rows of solar panels, continued to attract bees, butterflies and other pollinators. Their numbers were lower than in areas outside the solar farms, but the difference was less pronounced than in areas under constant shade.The researchers found that much of this variation was linked to how much shade the panels cast. Plants in continuous shade attracted fewer visits, but plants in partial shade between rows of panels still attracted pollinators. We found more pollinator activity in the sunnier spots.The researchers suspect the pattern may be partly due to the cooler conditions produced by solar panels. Pollinators tend to avoid cooler and shaded areas, creating what the study calls differentaround the panels.Shade can also affect the plants themselves. Reduced sunlight can decrease plant diversity and the quantity of pollen and nectar flowers produce. This means that even when pollinators do visit plants growing under panels, these plants may provide fewer resources.The research also examines whether the panels themselves may affect insect movement. The research suggests that solar installations may serve asfor butterflies that respond strongly to changes in their environment. Changes in soil moisture under the solar panels may also affect plant growth and insect feeding.The findings do not mean solar farms are inherently harmful to pollinators. Instead, they show that conditions within the same solar installation can vary depending on panel placement, vegetation and land management.The researchers also discovered something unexpected about land maintenance. Grazing led to lower pollinator abundance than mowing, the opposite of what the scientists expected.As Europe continues expanding solar power, researchers want future studies to examine pollinator behaviour in greater detail, including differences between individual species. More data could help scientists understand how solar panels alter local microclimates and how those changes affect pollination.The broader question is how solar farms can be designed and managed to becomewhile avoiding aThe French study suggests that solar installations can alter pollinator activity, but it also shows that their effects are not uniform, leaving room to explore how native vegetation and better land management could make these energy sites more compatible with bees, butterflies and other insects.
Article Summary: Solar farms produce clean energy, but the panels reshape the surrounding landscape. Research shows solar sites can encourage native plant growth. But the panels can also create shaded areas that affect plant-pollinator interactions. The French study suggests that solar installations can alter pollinator activity, but it also shows that their effects are not uniform.

Article Title: Explained: Xbox XP, company’s plan to expand gaming franchises into film, TV and theme parks

: Adapting game lore and characters into television shows, feature films, and linear media to engage wider audiences. Xbox products : Designing and manufacturing authentic merchandise that allows fans to celebrate their favorite gaming universes.

Building more ways to experience the worlds we love.

Our ambition at XBOX is to be the number one entertainment company in the world. This means growing our games into enduring franchises that entertain, inspire and connect people across every generation and across the globe.

That opportunity is why we’re creating XP.

It brings together capabilities that have existed across various teams at XBOX for years and aligns them behind a shared mission: helping our franchises reach more people, create deeper connections with players and new fans, and unlock new opportunities for these fandoms to grow around the world.

Great games remain at the center of these franchises and at the heart of XBOX. XP will partner with the best creative minds across our studios, along with trusted partners, to build on that foundation and create more ways for people to experience the worlds they love.

XBOX PICTURES: Bringing our worlds and characters to new audiences through film, television, and other forms of linear storytelling.

XBOX PRODUCTS: Creating products that are authentic to the fandom that allow fans to celebrate and express the franchises they love.

XBOX PLACES: Bringing communities together through live events, immersive experiences, attractions, broadcasts, and destinations.

I cannot imagine a better leader for this division and we are just getting started imagining what it will build.

Matthew Ball

As outlined in an internal communication from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, the newly established unit consolidates various capabilities that have operated across scattered teams for years, unifying them under a single strategic umbrella. In this article, we’ll explain what is it and how the company plans to expand its gaming division.Heading the division is newly appointed president Kayleen Walters, who will oversee Xbox's expansion across four dedicated focus areas: film and television, consumer retail products, live entertainment and brand collaborations.While Xbox stressed that producing top-tier video games remains the foundation of its business, the XP division will collaborate with studio teams and outside creatives across four formal investment branches.

Article Title: Top 3 US telecom companies lose billions after Elon Musk’s SpaceX announces spectrum purchase
Article Text:
Elon Musk’s SpaceX

SpaceX’s spectrum agreement

Shares of the three largest telecommunications carriers in the US dropped sharply, erasing roughly $45 billion in combined market value after Elon Musk ’s SpaceX announced a nationwide low-bandwidth spectrum purchase aimed at launching a Starlink mobile consumer service, reports have said. The announcement sparked immediate selling across wireless providers upon Wall Street’s opening bell, leading to historic single-day percentage declines for the established telecom giants.CNBC reported that Verizon Communications, the largest mobile network in the nation by subscribers, ended the day down 8.75% after tumbling 6.9% early in the session – its steepest one-day fall since July 2002. T-Mobile US plunged 13.27% after falling 9.6% at the open, marking its worst trading day since 2013. AT&T dropped 9.81% following an initial 8.4% drop, recording its sharpest market decline since 2000.SpaceX confirmed that it is acquiring licenses for up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800MHz band. The low-band frequencies provide an essential “coverage layer” for cellular networks. Since lower frequencies travel farther and pass more effectively through solid structures like building walls, the spectrum will allow Starlink Mobile signals to reach customer devices indoors.Following required approval from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), which manages and sells spectrum licenses, SpaceX plans to combine its direct-to-cell satellite services with a terrestrial network designed to connect phones and consumer devices in any location.SpaceX CEO Elon Musk described the spectrum acquisition as a “Very big deal”. While traditional cellular carriers dropped on the news, SpaceX shares rose 1.4% on Friday morning, adding approximately $30 billion to the company's valuation.Market analysts noted that securing low-band spectrum provides SpaceX with a clearer technical path toward commercial wireless deployment.“Buying spectrum is not a commitment to build a nationwide network. But this is the spectrum we thought SpaceX needed to make that option more credible— and less expensive,” analysts at Bernstein wrote in an investor research note following the announcement.
Article Summary: SpaceX confirmed that it is acquiring licenses for up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800MHz band. The low-band frequencies provide an essential “coverage layer” for cellular networks. Since lower frequencies travel farther and pass more effectively through solid structures like building walls, the spectrum will allow Starlink Mobile signals to reach customer devices indoors. While traditional cellular carriers dropped on the news, SpaceX shares rose 1.4% on Friday morning, adding approximately $30 billion to the company's valuation.
