Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 price, availability

Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 features

Dell Technologies has launched two rugged laptops, Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14, purpose-built for field workers who need technology that performs in the harshest conditions. From utility technicians troubleshooting infrastructure in extreme weather to public safety officers coordinating response efforts in the field, both devices are designed to keep workers productive when conditions are most demanding. The company said that Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 give IT teams a standardized, manageable platform that combines field-grade durability, AI-ready performance and advanced connectivity for large-scale field deployments.Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 are now available. The Dell Pro Rugged 14 (PR514260) is priced starting at Rs 2,65,990 and Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme (PR713260) price starts at Rs 3,36,990.Designed for workers across local governments, public safety, manufacturing, oil and gas, transportation and utilities, Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 are built to perform in the most demanding conditions.They are MIL-STD-810H certified for proven reliability with a temperature range of -20°F to 145°F, covering virtually any climate field workers might face. Displays feature gloved and water multi-touch support for use in personal protective equipment or wet conditions.Both laptops are powered by Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processors that offload AI and background tasks, keeping the system responsive during long shifts. They offer optional private 5G, Wi-Fi 7 and GPS for reliable connectivity and location tracking in remote locations. Hot-swappable batteries help ensure uninterrupted productivity for even the longest shifts. With up to a 5MP RGB+IR camera available on both laptops, workers can capture high-quality images and video in any environment.Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 are equipped with Rugged Control Center, built-in software that makes critical device settings easily accessible. From GPS module configuration to custom hardware shortcuts and device customization, it gives field workers the control they need to tailor their devices to the demands of the job.Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme is the most powerful and smallest 13-inch fully rugged AI PC, Dell says. Built for the harshest environments, it carries an IP66 rating for full protection against dust and water ingress and has been drop-tested from six feet (around 1.8 meters).It packs up to 64GB of LPDDR5X memory, removable SSD and self-encrypting drive options, giving organisations control over security and compliance in sensitive environments. It gets a 13.3-inch FHD display that reaches 1,400 nits of brightness for full readability in direct sunlight.Dell Pro Rugged 14 is built for professionals who need advanced performance in a portable, field-ready form factor. It’s the smallest and most powerful 14-inch semi-rugged AI PC, Dell says.It packs NVIDIA RTX PRO 500 Blackwell Generation Laptop GPU, LPCAMM2 memory up to 64GB, 14-inch 16:10 FHD display delivers up to 1,100 nits of brightness with a wider aspect ratio and a redesigned vehicle docking with quad passthrough for enhanced connectivity and compatibility with third-party docking solutions.
Article Summary: Dell Technologies has launched two rugged laptops, Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dellpro Rugged 14. The laptops are purpose-built for field workers who need technology that performs in the harshest conditions. The Dell Pro Pro Rugges 14 (PR514260) is priced starting at Rs 2,65,990 and the Dell ProPro Rugges 13 Extreme (PR713260) price starts at Rs 3,36,990.

Article Title: Microsoft makes major change to storage policy for Microsoft 365 Family, Premium and Pro plans; cuts OneDrive space across tiers: Here's how much storage subscribers will get now
Article Text:
Microsoft 365 Family storage drops from 6TB to 2TB

Microsoft 365 Family and Premium plans drop from 6TB to a shared 2TB OneDrive pool

Existing Microsoft 365 subscribers get the new OneDrive limit after May 2, 2027

Copilot and AI features can now be shared with everyone on the plan

Microsoft is changing how OneDrive storage works on its Microsoft 365 Family, Premium and Pro subscriptions, and for most households that means less space. Instead of every member getting a dedicated 1TB, these plans are moving to a single storage pool that everyone on the subscription draws from.For a Family or Premium plan shared by the maximum six people, that pool will be 2TB. Today, the same group gets 6TB between them. That is a two-thirds cut in total cloud storage, on plans where OneDrive space has long been a big reason people subscribe, even if they rarely open Word or Excel.The Pro plan gets a larger shared pool of 5TB, according to Microsoft's updated support document. Files, photos and documents stay private to each member by default, so sharing the space does not mean sharing what sits in it.What goes away is a guaranteed slice. If one member backs up years of phone videos, the others could run short. Any extra storage the account holder buys also lands in the common pool.Microsoft calls the new model more flexible. Unused space no longer sits idle, and a heavy user is no longer stuck at 1TB while others have room to spare. That suits a household with one power user. A family of four using 500GB each, however, will have to buy more space to keep what they already have.New and upgraded subscriptions moved to shared storage on October 8. Existing Family and Premium subscribers will switch at their first renewal on or after May 2, 2027, and Microsoft says they will be notified in detail before that. Moving to another eligible plan earlier, say from Family to Premium, could bring the change forward.Some existing users in eligible markets may get transitional bonus storage at the switch. Microsoft has not said how much, or who qualifies.The storage cut comes bundled with a perk. Until now, only the primary account holder on a Family or Premium plan could use Copilot and the AI features inside Office apps. Over the coming months, those benefits will extend to up to five other members, with controls to manage AI access for younger users.Separate limits for individual AI features will also give way to a single usage allowance, with the option to buy more. Households that lean on Copilot heavily could end up paying extra.The reaction has been sharp. A widely upvoted Reddit post is urging subscribers to switch off auto-renewal and cite the storage cut in Microsoft's cancellation survey, and some users say they already have. The change also arrives as AI data centres absorb more of the world's storage supply, with hard drive prices up 46% between September 2025 and January 2026. Microsoft has not linked the decision to costs.Families now get AI for everyone and less room for their files. They have until next May to decide if that is worth renewing.
Article Summary: Microsoft 365 Family and Premium plans drop from 6TB to a shared 2TB OneDrive pool. Existing Microsoft 365 subscribers get the new OneDrive limit after May 2, 2027. Copilot and AI features can now be shared with everyone on the plan.

Article Title: Meta bans TikTok in the US and Canada effective immediately; says we don't have to run ads from a competitor whose goal is to pull people off our apps
Article Text:
"We don't have to run ads from a competitor whose goal is to pull people off our apps,"

"Declining promotional services to a competitor is a normal business practice across industries. We will continue to compete on product quality and user experience."

Why has Meta banned TikTok advertisements

How will the advertising ban affect TikTok

Meta and TikTok face scrutiny over teen safety

Meta has banned advertisements from TikTok. According to a report by the news agency Reuters, Facebook and Instagram 's parent company has stopped all ads from TikTok's parent, ByteDance, across its platforms in the US and several other countries. This has re-escalated competition between the two social media companies.The report claims that the ban took effect immediately in the US, Canada, Egypt, Indonesia, Japan, Thailand and Vietnam. It also covers third-party advertisers running campaigns in these markets that link to TikTok and other ByteDance properties. Meta said it would keep competing on product quality and user experience, arguing it wasn't required to promote a rival trying to draw users away from its apps.Meta told Reuters.The decision escalates the rivalry between Meta and ByteDance. TikTok has emerged as a competitor to Meta's Facebook and Instagram in attracting users, creators and advertising revenue.The ban applies to ads promoting TikTok and other ByteDance properties, including third-party campaigns that direct users to those services in the affected countries.TikTok and ByteDance did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment on the decision. Bloomberg News first reported Meta's move.Meta's decision restricts ByteDance's ability to use its platforms to promote its services in the affected markets. However, TikTok's website does not support links that automatically open or log users into other social media apps. Users can still add links to their profiles that direct people to those platforms' websites.The move comes as Meta competes with TikTok for user attention and advertising spending. By restricting promotional campaigns from its rival, Meta is drawing a distinction between letting users access other platforms and selling ad space to promote them.The advertising dispute also comes amid wider scrutiny of social media companies over their impact on young users. Meta has urged TikTok and YouTube to follow measures it agreed to implement in August after reaching a settlement worth up to $18 billion with US states over claims related to social media harms to children.Under the agreement, Meta committed to introducing daily usage limits and nighttime restrictions for children using Facebook and Instagram, as well as strengthening measures to prevent them from accessing age-restricted content.TikTok has not yet publicly responded to Meta's campaign. But in September, the platform announced a settlement with Alabama that would require it to implement new usage caps and ramp up age-verification methods for users in that state. The claims resolved in the settlement were that TikTok endangered children and misled consumers about its safety.TikTok operates in the US as a majority American-owned joint venture following a deal intended to safeguard US user data and avert a ban on the service. The platform has more than 200 million users in the country.
Article Summary: Facebook and Instagram's parent company has stopped all ads from TikTok's parent, ByteDance. The ban took effect immediately in the US, Canada, Egypt, Indonesia, Japan, Thailand and Vietnam. It also covers third-party advertisers running campaigns in these markets that link to TikTok.

Article Title: Anthropic’s answer to AI-powered hacking is more AI, offering free Mythos security scans to open-source developers
Article Text:
Anthropic’s fix for AI hacking: more AI

Anthropic’s OSS Scanner flagged just one false alarm in testing

Only critical open-source projects can sign up for the free AI scans

Anthropic is putting its most powerful AI models, including Claude Mythos, to work on the open-source code that much of the internet is built on. The company has introduced OSS Scanner, a free, opt-in service that runs periodic AI security scans on eligible open-source projects and sends maintainers detailed vulnerability reports.The catch is that the reports are written entirely by AI. No human reviews or triages them before they reach a maintainer, and Anthropic admits some findings could be incorrect or invalid. Its argument is speed. With exploits now being built within minutes of a flaw surfacing, the company says projects that can find and fix bugs faster stand a better chance against attackers chasing the same weaknesses.Each report comes with a self-contained reproducer, an explanation of the bug, a bisection showing when it entered the code where possible, and a candidate patch when one is available. Anthropic spent several weeks testing the pipeline with dozens of projects. Its penetration testers checked 97 critical and high-severity findings across 48 projects, and 85 of them, or 88%, met the bar for its coordinated disclosure process. Of the other 12, 11 were real bugs already reported elsewhere, leaving a single false positive.Early testers back that up. wolfSSL said all but two of the 74 reports it received were valid, and five became CVEs.curl creator Daniel Stenberg said the scanner helped surface one of the worst curl vulnerabilities reported in the last few years.Enrolment is not open to every repository. Anthropic is borrowing its criteria from Google’s OSS-Fuzz, which has scanned open-source software with fuzzers since 2016, so only projects with a critical impact on infrastructure and user security will qualify, decided case by case. Core maintainers apply by submitting a pull request on GitHub. The service reportedly runs under Anthropic’s consumer terms, which allow inputs and outputs to be used for model training.OSS Scanner grows out of Project Glasswing. Over the past six months, Anthropic’s models flagged more than 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities in major software, but its team could manually verify only about 6,000. Language models now catch over 85% of vulnerabilities on the CyberGym benchmark, up from under 20% at the start of 2025.The stakes are familiar. Open-source projects are often run by unpaid volunteers, and the 2024 XZ Utils backdoor showed how a single compromised library could expose millions of systems. Anthropic expects attackers to keep the upper hand for the next two years, until AI catches bugs before they ship.
Article Summary: OSS Scanner runs periodic AI security scans on eligible open-source projects. No human reviews or triages them before they reach a maintainer, and Anthropic admits some findings could be incorrect or invalid. Anthropic spent several weeks testing the pipeline with dozens of projects. Its penetration testers checked 97 critical and high-severity findings across 48 projects.
